Pressure cleaning in Melbourne

High pressure cleaning, at a pressure the surface will take

Hard outdoor surfaces across Melbourne: driveways, concrete, exposed aggregate, paving, outdoor tile, brick, decking, fencing and paths. Flat work runs under a rotary surface cleaner so the finish comes up even instead of striped.

  • Pressure matched to the material
  • Priced per square metre
  • Test patch before anything unusual
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Pressure and surface cleaning

What it is

Pressure cleaning uses water at pressure to lift what is sitting on a hard surface: biological film, traffic grime, leaf tannin, moss and general weathering. It is a mechanical clean, so it works on anything the material can physically take, and it does nothing at all for a stain that has gone into the material.

The skill is not in the pressure. Any machine will take 4,000 psi off the shelf. The skill is knowing that the same nozzle which cleans a concrete driveway in one pass will cut a groove in softwood decking, blow the sand out of paver joints, strip the face off a sand-finished render and dull a glazed outdoor tile permanently. The pressure, the nozzle angle, the distance and the chemistry all change per material, and most of the damage we are called to repair was done by someone treating every surface as if it were concrete.

Pressure by material

The same machine, set up differently for every surface

This is the part that decides whether a surface comes up clean or comes up damaged. Figures are working ranges, not a specification, and condition moves them.

What each surface takes, and what goes wrong when it is cleaned at the wrong setting. Anything not listed gets a test patch first.
  Typical approach What happens if it is overdone
Broom finished concrete High pressure under a rotary surface cleaner, straight water for most jobs Very hard to damage, but a held wand leaves visible stripes and swirl marks
Exposed aggregate Moderate pressure, surface cleaner, pre-treatment for biological growth Stones loosen out of the matrix and the slab starts shedding gravel
Clay and concrete pavers Moderate pressure, then joint sand replaced afterwards Jointing sand is blasted out, pavers rock underfoot and weeds come back faster
Outdoor porcelain and glazed tile Low pressure with a cleaning solution doing the work, soft brush on grout The glaze micro-scratches and the tile holds dirt worse than before
Brickwork Low to moderate, kept off the mortar lines, checked for perished pointing Mortar washes out of the joints, which is a repointing job, not a cleaning one
Timber decking Low pressure, fan nozzle, always with the grain The soft spring growth erodes between the hard grain and the board furs up
Painted or rendered walls Not pressure cleaned at all. These are soft washed Paint lifts, render face erodes and water is driven in behind the sheet

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Surfaces we clean

Everything outside that will take mechanical cleaning

Driveways

The most common single job. Concrete, aggregate and paved driveways carry traffic film, tyre marks and oil, and they are the first thing anyone sees.

Concrete and exposed aggregate

Paths, slabs, alfresco areas and pool surrounds. Porous, so biological growth sits down in the surface rather than on it.

Paving and patios

Clay, concrete and bluestone paving. Cleaning is half the job, re-sanding the joints afterwards is the other half.

Pool surrounds

Usually the dampest hard surface on a property, so it grows the most and is the one that matters most underfoot.

Brick and masonry

Facades, retaining walls, fences and piers, with the pointing checked before anything is turned on.

Decking and timber

Low pressure only, with the grain, and usually the step before an oil or stain is reapplied.

Fencing

Colorbond, brick and timber boundary fencing, which picks up the most growth on the shaded side.

Paths and hard surfaces

Footpaths, crossovers, side access, bin areas and anything else that has gone dark and slippery.

Commercial hardstand

Car parks, loading areas and service yards, scheduled around trading. Priced and managed through commercial exterior cleaning.

Why flat work runs under a surface cleaner

A pressure washing wand cleans in an arc. Held by a person, that arc overlaps unevenly, which is where the tiger stripes across a badly cleaned driveway come from. They are not dirt, they are a record of where the wand was.

A rotary surface cleaner is a shrouded head with two or three jets spinning under it at a fixed height. It holds the same distance and the same overlap across the whole slab, so the finish is even, it uses less water per square metre, and it keeps the spray and the dislodged material contained rather than throwing it up a wall or across a window.

Wands still have their place: edges, steps, risers, corners and vertical work. Most flat jobs are a surface cleaner for the field and a wand for the detail, in that order.

Scope

What a pressure clean covers, and what it does not

Included in a hard surface clean

Standard on every job at no extra cost.

  • Pre-wet and pre-treatment of the surface where growth is present
  • Rotary surface cleaner across all flat work, wand detailing on edges and steps
  • Moving pots, bins and light furniture, and putting them back
  • Rinse down of adjacent walls, glazing and garden beds where overspray lands
  • Run off directed away from garden beds and pools
  • Grates and drains cleared of the material we dislodge
  • A walk around with you at the end before we pack up

Quoted separately or not done

These are real jobs, just not part of a standard clean.

  • Stains that have gone into the material. That is restoration
  • Sealing. It needs a clean dry surface, so it is a separate visit
  • Paver joint re-sanding, where joints are empty before we start
  • Render, painted and cladded walls. Those are soft washed
  • Roof surfaces, which carry their own access and tile condition risk
  • Repointing, crack repair, concrete grinding and resurfacing
  • Weed and moss killing as a standalone service without a clean

How the job runs

Four stages, usually one visit

STEP 01

Walk the site

Surfaces identified, condition noted, pointing and joints checked, water and power located, and anything fragile flagged before a hose comes off the truck.

STEP 02

Pre‑treat

Biological growth gets a solution and dwell time. This is what kills it rather than relocating it, and it is why a pre-treated slab stays clean months longer than one that was only blasted.

STEP 03

Clean

Surface cleaner across the field, wand for edges, steps and detail. Vertical surfaces worked top down so nothing is cleaned twice.

STEP 04

Rinse and check

Everything adjacent rinsed, drains cleared, furniture back, and a walk around together. If something has not come up we say so then rather than leaving you to find it.

Go straight to the surface

Ten hard surface pages, one per material

Each one covers what that material takes, what it costs to clean and what tends to go wrong with it.

Driveway cleaningThe most requested surface, and usually the one setting the impression of the whole property. Concrete cleaningSlabs, paths and alfresco areas in broom finished and smooth concrete. Exposed aggregate cleaningPorous, decorative and easy to damage with too much pressure. Paving and patio cleaningClay, concrete and stone paving, with the joints dealt with afterwards. Outdoor tile cleaningPorcelain, travertine and glazed tile, where the glaze sets the limit. Pool surround cleaningThe dampest hard surface on most properties, and the one underfoot wet. Brick cleaningFacades, retaining walls and piers, with the pointing checked first. Deck and timber cleaningLow pressure, with the grain, usually before re-oiling. Fence cleaningColorbond, brick and timber boundary fencing. Path and hard surface cleaningFootpaths, crossovers, side access and bin areas.

Questions

What people ask before booking a hard surface clean

How much does pressure cleaning cost in Melbourne?

Hard surface work is priced on area and condition rather than by the hour. A single car driveway in reasonable condition is a different job from the same slab after ten years under a gum tree, so the figure moves with how much pre-treatment and how many passes it needs.

We quote from photos for most residential work. Send the suburb, roughly the size, and a picture of the worst part rather than the best, and you get a fixed price for the work instead of a rate with an open end on it.

Will pressure cleaning damage my driveway?

Not if the pressure suits the material. Concrete is very hard to damage. Exposed aggregate can be made to shed stones, pavers can have their joint sand stripped out, and outdoor tile glazes can be dulled permanently. Those are the surfaces where the setting matters, and they are cleaned at lower pressure with the chemistry doing more of the work.

Anything unusual gets a test patch in a spot you will not see, so you can look at the result before the whole surface is committed.

Do you use chemicals, and are they safe around plants and pets?

Yes, on most jobs. Biological growth is not removed by water alone, it is only moved, which is why a blasted slab greens up again within months. A pre-treatment with dwell time kills it at the root.

Garden beds are pre-wet and rinsed, run off is directed away from them and away from pools, and pets are better kept inside while we are working and until the surface has dried.

How long does it stay clean?

In Melbourne, a pre-treated surface in reasonable sun usually holds up for two to three years before it needs doing again. A shaded south-facing slab under trees can start to go within twelve months, because the growth has ideal conditions and keeps being re-seeded from above.

If that is your situation, sealing the surface after the clean is what changes the number, because growth and stains cannot get into a sealed surface in the first place.

What is the difference between pressure cleaning and soft washing?

Pressure does the work in one, chemistry does the work in the other.

  • Pressure cleaning is for hard surfaces that can take it: concrete, aggregate, paving, brick, hardstand.
  • Soft washing is for anything that cannot: render, paint, cladding, weatherboard and most roof surfaces. The pressure is barely above a garden hose and a solution does the cleaning.

Most houses need both, on different parts of the same property.

Do I need to be home?

No, as long as we have access to the surfaces, an outside tap and a power point. Plenty of residential jobs are done while people are at work. We will send through what it looked like at the end.

Do you do commercial sites and car parks?

Yes. Hardstand, car parks, loading areas, service yards and shopfront surrounds, scheduled around when the site is quiet rather than when it suits us. That work is quoted and managed as commercial exterior cleaning, usually on a cycle rather than job by job.

Even finish, no tiger stripes

Priced by the square metre, not by the hour

Driveways, concrete, aggregate, paving, tile, brick, decking and fencing across Melbourne. Pre-treated so it stays clean, and sealed afterwards if you want it to last.
